status: unpublished: the cutter itself was unpublishable until AER-1142 (per AER-1140's ruling) reworked it -- a uniform 3x3-degree native-tile window busted the 200 MB cap on its own, and separately captured only 14% of Raleigh's water at 160 NM. The rework (tarball-gated cap, concentric per-mip-level terrain cut, per-layer derived footprints, an anti-vacuity coverage test) is done and covered by tests/tools/test_make_map_perf_fixture.py against synthetic packs. AER-1143's amendment additionally widened the water/highway derivation to the widest of every widget geometry the perf suite asserts against (not just one hard-coded widget) and made every cut pack declare its own footprint.json (bbox + (w,h,ownship_position,range_nm) envelope per layer) so a consumer test can compare instead of re-deriving. What is still missing is a `make_map_perf_fixture.py cut --scene <s> --publish` run against the REAL production terrain/water/highway/navaid packs plus R2 write credentials (CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN/CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID) -- neither is available in the pyEfis dev sandbox this manifest was authored in, and cutting/publishing the real packs is AVIONICS-DATA's (AER-1134), not this tool's. fetch_fixture() raises PerfFixtureUnavailable rather than silently no-oping while this is null.
